correctness.rationale: Independently rebuilt the 40 tetrahedra from the public Lutz facet table (exact same 40 labelled facets as in assigned verify.py), yielding f=(11,51,80,40). A separately written GF(2) bit-vector boundary reduction finds rank ∂2=40 and rank ∂3=39 on 80 triangles, hence H2 dimension one. For all vertex subsets of sizes 1..6, independently constructed complete local 2-cycle spaces and reduced them modulo global 3-boundaries; numbers of supporting subsets are 0,0,0,0,0,20. Every minimizing induced complex has six vertices, fifteen edges, ten triangles, no tetrahedron, links single cycles and χ=1, so is RP2. Exhaustive degree/triangle-compatible vertex bijections with final facet preservation gave 48 automorphisms and 12+8 carrier orbit sizes with the specified two representatives. All searches over 11 vertices or labelled permutations finite and exhaustive; this is mod-two homology, not integral H2.

value.rationale: The vertex-minimal triangulation of a standard manifold has a canonical nonzero mod-two middle homology class. Knowing its sharp minimum vertex support and exactly which minimal induced RP2 subcomplexes realize it, including complete orbit decomposition, is a natural and usable invariant for triangulation topology, embedding constraints and symmetry comparisons rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.

final_claim: In the specified 40-facet 11-vertex triangulation of RP^3, nonzero mod-two H2 has minimum induced vertex support six, exactly 20 six-vertex carriers all triangulating RP2, and 48 automorphisms split them into orbits 12 and 8.
limitations: The complete original historical 48-page Lutz paper and older computational appendices were not inspected in full; an unindexed induced-RP2 census remains possible.
